subject: Sparkline pilot: eval playlist, model recommendations, and quality guardrails
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Hassan <amira@sparklinehealth.com>, Roberto Diaz <rdiaz@sparklinehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-09T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + immediate next steps from today’s pilot discovery

Hi Amira / Roberto —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned:

Summary of the call:
- Use case: triage-assist for intake nurses + clinical summarization for PCP handoffs.
- Primary success metrics: top-1 accuracy of triage suggestion (threshold 88%), and F1 on clinical entity extraction for summaries (target 0.82).
- Data available: 12k de-identified intake notes (CSV format), 250 annotated summaries for scorer alignment.

Redwood pilot proposal (short):
1) Short bench run (48–72 hrs): run 3 candidate models on a 2k-sample slice to compare latency and quality.
2) Full eval (~2 weeks): run selected model on 10k records with scoring rubric and report.
3) Regression guardrails: establish prompt suite and golden examples + automatic quality alerts.

Immediate asks from Sparkline: please share a 1–2k sample CSV export with the following columns: record_id, intake_text, structured_fields (JSON allowed), and gold_summary (if available). We attached a sample CSV and kickoff notes that show Redwood’s preferred format.

Recommended starting models (based on the call):
- redwood-rlhf-13b (quantized) — balance of generation quality and cost
- redwood-instruct-7b-q4 — faster, good for high-throughput triage
- open-eval-70b-8k — if Sparkline wants max recall for entity extraction (higher cost)

Next steps / Owners: 
- Amira: share 2k sample by Tue 8/11 (owner: customer)
- Ben + Jordan: prepare model shortlist and perf/baseline script (owner: ben.carter)
- Marcus: propose scoring rubric and automated alert thresholds (owner: marcus.lin)

Attachments: sparkline-kickoff-notes.pdf, pilot-dataset-sample.csv, redwood-recommendations.md

Thanks — I’ll stand up the short bench once we have the sample.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Amira Hassan <amira@sparklinehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Roberto Diaz <rdiaz@sparklinehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-10T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + immediate next steps from today’s pilot discovery

Thanks Ben — and thanks everyone on the call. Quick notes: we can provide a 2k sample by end of day Tuesday (8/11).

Couple of clarifying Qs before we upload:
1) For structured_fields column — is free-form JSON okay for mixed clinical codes + checkboxes?
2) For the gold_summary column — some records won’t have a human-written summary. Is that ok for the bench run?

Also — cost sensitivity: our procurement asks that the initial bench stay <$1k for the POC. Can you confirm rough burn for the 2k short bench with the three candidate models?

We’ll upload to the Drive folder and share link to the S3 presigned if needed.

—Amira
Product Lead, Sparkline Health
amira@sparklinehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Hassan <amira@sparklinehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-10T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + immediate next steps from today’s pilot discovery

Amira — great, thank you. Answers inline and a few concrete cost and model notes: 

1) structured_fields: free-form JSON is fine — we’ll validate and provide a simple schema check script.
2) gold_summary: OK if some records are missing — for the bench we’ll run two modes: (a) scoring against gold where available, (b) qualitative scorer set for samples without gold.

Estimated cost for the 2k short bench (approx):
- redwood-instruct-7b-q4: ~$120 (fastest)
- redwood-rlhf-13b (q4): ~$320
- open-eval-70b-8k: ~$860
Total (all three): ~ $1,300. We can scope to two models to keep under $1k (suggest 7b + 13b).

We’ve uploaded a lightweight runner and the prompt set we intend to use to the Drive link in related_links (please see the folder). The prompt set includes: triage prompt family, clinical-summary prompt family, and few-shot examples / negative examples for hallucination tests.

Marcus — looping you in to propose the scoring rubric and threshold rules.

Ben

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Amira Hassan <amira@sparklinehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-11T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Scoring rubric and regression guardrails (draft)

Hi Amira / Roberto —

Draft scoring plan for the pilot bench:

1) Primary metrics:
- Triage accuracy (top-1) — compare model suggestion to gold triage_label where available. Weight: 40%
- Summary F1 (entity-level nutritive) — custom entity set defined by Sparkline (examples requested). Weight: 35%
- Hallucination penalty — automated n-gram overlap checks + scorer reviewer flags. Weight: 15%
- Latency SLA — p95 token latency under 650ms for interactive triage route. Weight: 10%

2) Data split for bench: 2k sample -> 70/15/15 split for initial comparison / validation / guardrail checks.

3) Quality guardrails:
- Prefix/KV caching disabled for bench to avoid caching bias.
- A prompt mutation set to surface hallucination sensitivity (5 variants per prompt).
- Alerting: fail if hallucination penalty > 0.15 on validation slice.

4) Data format checklist (we need a confirm from Sparkline):
- UTF-8 CSV, comma-separated, header row with: record_id,intake_text,structured_fields,gold_summary,triage_label
- If structured_fields is JSON, provide a sample schema or 10 example records.

Ben — I’ll produce a scoring rubric doc and a small reference scorer (python) once Amira confirms the sample format.

Marcus Lin
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Amira Hassan <amira@sparklinehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Roberto Diaz <rdiaz@sparklinehealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Scoring rubric and regression guardrails (draft)

Thanks Marcus — that rubric looks reasonable and aligns with our internal priorities. We’ve uploaded the 2k sample to the Drive folder (link above) and also put a presigned S3 link in the folder for the full dataset export. Notes on the sample:
- structured_fields uses a small JSON blob (code + flags), sample schema included in the folder.
- ~60% of records have gold_summary; triage_label present for 95% of records.

We approve starting the 2k bench with redwood-instruct-7b-q4 + redwood-rlhf-13b (keep the 70/15/15 split). Please confirm start time and expected deliverables (bench report + scoring CSV + top failure examples) and keep the initial burn under $1k by avoiding the 70b run.

Amira
